paper_title: Adaptive Testing for LLM Evaluation: A Psychometric Alternative to Static Benchmarks
reason: 이 논문은 ATLAS라는 IRT 기반 적응형 평가 방법론을 제안한다. 기존 벤치마크(WinoGrande, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, GSM8K, ARC)의 문항을 보정한 item bank를 사용하고, 문항 수를 줄이면서도 능력 추정의 정밀도를 유지하는 것이 핵심이다. 새로운 과제나 문항을 가진 재사용 가능한 벤치마크라기보다 평가 방법론에 가깝다. 보정된 item bank와 코드는 공개되어 있지만, 기반이 되는 벤치마크는 이미 영어 인벤토리에 있거나 별도로 다룰 대상이며 평가 대상 과제 자체에 실질적 변경이 없다. 한국어 과제도 포함되어 있지 않다. 따라서 중복이며 실질적 변경이 없다고 판단하여 제외한다.

screening.paper_title: Adaptive Testing for LLM Evaluation: A Psychometric Alternative to Static Benchmarks
screening.abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) typically requires thousands of benchmark items, making the process expensive, slow, and increasingly impractical at scale. Existing evaluation protocols rely on average accuracy over fixed item sets, treating all items as equally informative despite substantial variation in difficulty and discrimination. We introduce ATLAS, an adaptive testing framework based on Item Response Theory (IRT) that estimates model ability using Fisher information-guided item selection. ATLAS reduces the number of required items by up to 90% while maintaining measurement precision. For instance, it matches whole-bank ability estimates using only 41 items (0.157 MAE) on HellaSwag (5,600 items). We further reconstruct accuracy from ATLAS's ability estimates and find that reconstructed accuracies closely match raw accuracies across all five benchmarks, indicating that ability $θ$ preserves the global performance structure. At the same time, $θ$ provides finer discrimination within accuracy-equivalent models: among more than 3,000 evaluated models, 23-31% shift by more than 10 rank positions, and models with identical accuracies receive meaningfully different ability estimates. Code and calibrated item banks are available at https://github.com/Peiyu-Georgia-Li/ATLAS.git.
